items.title: MIT study finds AI-generated images often can't be traced to specific training data ("attribution decay")
items.summary_en: MIT CSAIL researchers, with Zheng Dai as lead author, describe a phenomenon they call 'attribution decay': as generative image models train on larger datasets, the influence of any single training example on a given output shrinks toward zero. In controlled experiments removing a specific image, all works by one artist, or all photos of one person from a training set, the generated output was often unchanged once the dataset was large enough, suggesting no individual example could be identified as responsible for a specific output. The researchers frame this as relevant to ongoing copyright and attribution debates around AI-generated art.
